title: Cross-org window coalescence glitch during hot policy reload causing duplicate meter increments
creator: Evan Chen
description: When the rate policy evaluator performs a hot reload of per-org/per-route rules while shard coalescer is merging time windows, some in-flight requests are double-accounted. The issue appears during high-throughput reconfiguration (canary or admin edits) and leads to short bursts of overcharging and premature throttles for affected API keys. This ticket tracks reproducing, root cause analysis, mitigation, and a robust fix to avoid duplicate increments during policy reloads and shard rebalances.
reproduction_steps: Stand up a two-shard route serving a mix of org-scoped and key-scoped policies with short burst windows (e.g., 1s sampling, 10s burst).
Load generator: sustained 150% of typical throughput to both shards and then trigger a policy edit that updates a route-level burst credit for the same org.
Observe metering logs on both shards and the coalescer: look for the same request UUID being accounted twice in adjacent windows after the reload.
Confirm via billing proto logs that duplicate increments map to the same tokenized request id and happen within the boundary of the hot-reload window (typically 200-800ms).
timeline: 2026-03-10: Incident reported by on-call after customer alerting showed unexplained burst credit consumption.
2026-03-11: Initial triage — reproduced in staging with policy hot-reload and confirmed duplicate meter increments on coalescer logs.
2026-03-12: Scoped potential causes: window coalescer race during rule swap, shard reconcilers replay, and policy evaluator broadcast duplication.
2026-03-13: Short mitigation deployed: disable hot-reload broadcast for affected route group and reverted a recent canary policy push (rollback).
2026-03-14: Engineering lead assigned, detailed instrumentation added, and ticket opened for full fix and tests.
investigation_notes: Duplicate accounting only observed when (a) a policy change is broadcast while in-flight requests straddle window boundaries and (b) coalescer re-emit path merges partial window deltas.
Logs show two different components (local shard aggregator and remote reconcile handler) emitting meter-increment events with the same request id but different origin tags after a reload.
Hypothesis: policy hot-reload handshake triggers a transient re-evaluation that causes the request to be requeued to the meter pipeline without dedup metadata set.
We saw no evidence of KV-store corruption. The issue is timing/race-related and deterministic under synthetic load with short windows.
root_cause: Race between policy hot-reload broadcast and the shard-level window coalescer's flush/remerge path. The hot-reload path re-evaluates and re-emits accounting for in-flight requests, and because the dedup token was not propagated through the reconcile handler for that code path, the same request led to two separate increments across the coalesced windows.
mitigations: Immediate: Roll back the canary policy push and temporarily disable live policy broadcasts for routes with sub-second windows (deployed 2026-03-13).
Short-term: Add gating on the reconcile handler to ignore repeated accounting events within a 1s dedup window keyed by request UUID and shard-epoch.
Long-term: Ensure dedup token propagation through all policy-eval-to-metering code paths and add unit + integration tests for hot-reload scenarios.
proposed_fix: 1) Add an immutable dedup token on request context that survives policy re-evaluation and is included in all meter-increment events. 2) Change the coalescer merge path to detect matching request UUIDs within the same logical window and discard duplicates. 3) Harden the policy broadcast handshake to mark in-flight requests as 'hot-reload-guarded' so they are only emitted once per epoch.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate meter-increments observed in staging under synthetic load that previously triggered duplication (same load/reload pattern).
Integration test that performs 1k hot-reloads while running a load generator shows zero duplicate increments for the same request UUIDs over 10 runs.
Telemetry: Per-route duplicate-meter metric returns to baseline (0) for affected routes after rollout.
Post-deploy smoke: Sanity billing compare job shows no regression vs. control cluster for 72h.
notes_for_release: When shipping runtime-1.25 include feature flag to enable dedup for hot-reload in <runtime-config>. Default off until full integration tests pass. Coordinate with SRE for staggered rollout to Dedicated clusters.
followups: Add chaos test that kills reconcile handlers mid-window and asserts no duplicate accounting (owner: Platform QA).
Evaluate whether similar dedup tokens are needed for shadow-metering and billing-backfill paths (owner: Billing team).
